newsitem.title: india: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT DIVIDED OVER NEXT PRESIDENT

With President Shankar Dayal Sharma's term coming to an end in July, a section of the United Front (UF) government has begun mobilising support to ensure Vice President K.R. Narayanan takes over. This became all the more urgent for this section because it felt another section was toying with the idea of having a north Indian, also a member of a minority community, to balance the south Indian prime minister. Sources said the information minister was asked to sound out the governor of Karnataka, Khurshid Alam Khan, son-in-law of former president Zakir Hussain, for the job.
The Pioneer
GOVERNMENT FINDS WAYS TO PUNCTURE CONGRESS DRIVE

The United Front (UF) government seemed to have arrived at a set of internal compromises, while closing ranks against an aggressive Congress party in the run-up to the budget session of parliament. Under pressure from its Left constituents, it referred the new broadcasting bill to a sub-committee. It also deferred a decision on sugar subsidies as well as revising the price of sugar in the public distribution system in view of impending polls in several states. Two other partners, the TMC and DMK successfully pre-empted moves to project the Karnataka governor as a candidate for the next presidential election. The Economic Times
ELECTIONS HOLD BACK SUGAR PRICE HIKE

The cabinet deferred its decision on sugar subsidy and a hike in levy sugar price until the completion of the forthcoming state elections. This decision, which was being viewed as politically sensitive, was discussed at least twice in the last fortnight. If rising production costs of sugar do not translate into a hike in prices, the exchequer may have an estimated 600 million rupee subsidy burden a month on its hands.
BOURSE INDEX RISES 127 PTS DESPITE LETDOWN

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's package of market-friendly measures continued to elude the markets but did little to rein in speculators' enthusiasm on the bourses. Frenzied buying by speculators took the Bombay bourse sensitive index (Sensex) up 127 points, or 3.7 percent, to 3,562 points. The sharp rise came on heavy speculative buying in counters like Reliance, State Bank, Tata Steel, ITC, Telco and ACC. The Sensex has risen roughly 15 percent this year, ever since the prime minister promised market-friendly policy initiatives.
STEEL MAJORS TO SKETCH FLOOR PRICE STRATEGY

The steel manufacturers will meet to fork out a joint pricing strategy for a minimum floor price. This has become necessary for the collective survival of the industry as the ongoing discount war among steel companies is threatening to wipe out their bottom lines. Saddled with huge inventories, all the players have been offering huge discounts to woo customers. Input costs have increased by over 20 percent in the past one year without any real increase in price. The depressed margins are expected to take a toll on profits in the current fiscal.
Financial Express
DERESERVATION MOOTED IN SMALL SCALE SECTOR

The expert panel on small enterprises mooted highly debatable and sweeping reforms in the small-scale sector to make it globally competitive. The committee recommended abolition of the reservation policy, scrapping foreign equity limit and enhancing the investment limit to 30 million rupees for the sector. The government would study the recommendations and implement the non-controversial ones as soon as possible, the Industry Minister said. The recommendations would be sent to all industrial associations for their comments, he added.
MINISTRIES TRADE CHARGES OVER TATA-SIA CASE

The Industry Ministry accused the Civil Aviation Ministry of misreporting cabinet proceedings on the new aviation policy. The ministry has taken up the decision and the fate of the Tata-Singapore Airlines proposal with the cabinet secretariat, sources said. The aviation secretary had said that the issue of equity participation by foreign airlines and airports in joint ventures was referred back to the Industry Ministry. But sources denied that the 24 billion rupee Tata-SIA venture was referred back to the Industry Ministry for reconsideration.
Business Standard
VOLKSWAGEN TO INVEST $100 MLN

Volkswagen will invest $100 million in India to produce medium and top-of-the line cars by the year-end. It would be a joint venture with 50 percent equity by a local automobile major, a senior Volkswagen official said. The German automobile giant is talking to two leading car manufacturers, and a final decision would be taken in a couple of weeks. Volkswagen plans to set up its production plant in Bangalore.
BINDING COMMITMENT TO BE REVIEWED IN 2000

The government has decided to stick to an offer to make a binding commitment of 25 percent foreign equity in telecommunication service companies at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) negotiations. It has however offered to review the offer in the year 2000. Although 49 percent foreign equity is allowed in telecommunication, the government does not want to bind itself at the WTO on the decision. Any changes in the offer during deliberations at the negotiating group on basic telecoms, which will discuss offers by various countries, was ruled out by the communication minister. The Observer
THREE FOREIGN INVESTORS APPROVED FOR DEBT FUNDS

The bourse regulator (SEBI) allowed three foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to invest in 100 percent debt funds. This investment route was approved by the government and SEBI in December. The clearance was for investments totalling $203 million in the next three months. The three FIIs, which were approved for investment in debt funds, include Chesor International through their sub-account New India Investment, Credit Suisse Asset Management through Professional Services Insurance incorporated in Bermuda and J. Henry Schroder Bank through Fixed Income Portfolio Mauritius.
Business Line
DUNLOP CLAIMS ALL'S WELL IN COMPANY

Dunlop management said its managing director continued to enjoy the confidence of chairman Manu Chhabria. Management conceded the firm faced operational problems in the recent past because of limited availability of working capital from funding agencies as also certain environmental issues. But, workers and managers of the company were jointly trying to overcome the difficulties, it added. There was, however, no mention of the reports suggesting the management and unionised employees' resentment of Chhabria's alleged misbehaviour with three senior company executives and his intention to induct his daughter on the board.
GOVERNMENT TO ACT AGAINST WILD CAPITAL MARKET SWINGS

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda indicated the government would not allow wild fluctuations in the capital markets, caused by speculators. He, however, said the government would announce a few measures, as promised, prior to the World Economic Forum meeting at Davos, Switzerland. The prime minister also asked for more details from industrialists and economists on the stock market fluctuations witnessed in the past few weeks.
